findings.issue_text: [High/bug] AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JVM default keystore provider, typically SUN, instead of Bouncy Castle, breaking callers that require BC algorithms
[Medium/bug] ASN1Decoder.readSequence() treats the -1 length for indefinite-length encoding as an empty sequence instead of consuming elements through the end-of-contents marker

[Medium/api] Adding abstract CryptoProvider.order() breaks binary compatibility with third-party implementations and can cause AbstractMethodError during provider discovery; it should be a default method

[Low/performance] AuthzClientCryptoProvider unnecessarily populates and discards two encoders before creating identical encoders for the returned sequence, adding allocations and encoding work to every ECDSA conversion

[Medium/test_gap] ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses one unspecified default EC keypair and tests only conversion round trips without JCA signature verification, allowing mutually inverse conversion bugs and ES384/ES512 interoperability failures to go undetected

goldens.comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)

Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses one unspecified default EC keypair and tests only conversion round trips without JCA signature verification, allowing mutually inverse conversion bugs and ES384/ES512 interoperability failures to go undetected

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that ECDSAAlgorithmTest only tests round-trip conversion (asn1derToConcatenatedRS -> concatenatedRSToASN1DER -> asn1derToConcatenatedRS) without verifying the actual signature using JCA. The test uses a single KeyPairGenerator.getInstance('EC').genKeyPair() without specifying curve parameters, so it only tests with the default curve. The test doesn't verify that the converted signature can actually be verified by the JCA Signature class, which means mutually inverse bugs could go undetected. This is a legitimate test gap for newly added crypto conversion code.
